note: Assertions are graded against the proposal each run wrote to outputs/files/<repo-relative-path>. Each one maps to a numbered Hard rule in SKILL.md, so a failure points at the exact rule the run broke.

assertions.rule: Where does the port interface go? — server-local ports live beside their adapter
assertions.text: A notification port interface is declared, and since nothing outside server/ names it, it lives beside its adapter (adapters/notifier/) rather than widening the client-mirrored vendor/shared surface

assertions.rule: Layer map — infrastructure
assertions.text: The concrete implementation (the HTTP POST to the webhook) lives in a file under server/src/adapters/

assertions.rule: Hard rule 3 — no direct SDK/HTTP construction in a service
assertions.text: No service.ts performs the HTTP call itself (no fetch/axios/undici/WebClient inside modules/*/service.ts)

assertions.rule: Hard rule 6 — compose only at the root
assertions.text: The adapter is wired in server/src/platform/container.ts

assertions.rule: Hard rule 6 — a service receives its dependencies
assertions.text: The service receives the notifier as an injected dependency and does not construct the adapter itself (no `new <Adapter>(` in service.ts)

assertions.rule: Config/secrets convention
assertions.text: The webhook URL comes from config/secrets, not a hardcoded literal URL in the service or adapter

assertions.rule: Hard rule 4 — routes are thin
assertions.text: routes.ts contains no Drizzle/SQL query (no drizzle-orm import, no db.select/count/sql usage)

assertions.rule: Layer map — infrastructure
assertions.text: The aggregation query lives in repository.ts

assertions.rule: Layer map — application
assertions.text: A service.ts orchestrates: the route calls the service, the service calls the repository

assertions.rule: Decision rule — contracts live in vendor/shared/contracts
assertions.text: The response shape is defined as a Zod schema under server/src/vendor/shared/contracts/

assertions.rule: Hard rule 5 — map at the boundary
assertions.text: Row -> DTO conversion happens in helpers.ts and no raw Drizzle row is handed to HTTP

assertions.rule: Tenancy (server/CLAUDE.md)
assertions.text: The query is workspace-scoped (filters on workspace_id / uses the request's workspace context)

assertions.rule: Hard rule 2 — keep the core pure
assertions.text: No file under reviewer-core/ imports Octokit or any GitHub/HTTP SDK

assertions.rule: Hard rule 2 — reviewer-core performs zero I/O
assertions.text: No file under reviewer-core/ performs network or filesystem I/O (no fetch/axios/node:fs/node:https)

assertions.rule: Hard rule 3 — external systems reached via ports
assertions.text: The GitHub read happens on the server side through the existing GitHubClient port resolved from the Container (no ad-hoc Octokit construction)

assertions.rule: Hard rule 1 — dependencies point inward
assertions.text: The open-PR/conflict data enters reviewer-core as plain injected input (a field on the review input or an injected port), not fetched by reviewer-core itself

assertions.rule: Hard rule 2 — the core stays dependency-free
assertions.text: No GitHub/HTTP dependency is added to reviewer-core/package.json

assertions.rule: Where does the port interface go?
assertions.text: A cache port interface is declared beside its adapter under server/src/adapters/ and NOT pushed into the client-mirrored vendor/shared/adapters.ts

assertions.rule: Hard rule 3 — no direct SDK construction outside an adapter
assertions.text: The Redis client is constructed only inside server/src/adapters/ — no `new Redis(...)` in a service, repository, or route

assertions.rule: Hard rule 6 — compose only at the root
assertions.text: The cache is resolved from platform/container.ts and has a ContainerOverrides slot so tests can swap it

assertions.rule: Hard rule 1 — the inside codes against the port
assertions.text: The caller codes against the cache port, not against Redis types (no ioredis/Redis import outside adapters/)

assertions.rule: Config convention
assertions.text: The Redis connection string comes from config/env, not a hardcoded literal

assertions.rule: Hard rule 1 — dependencies point inward only
assertions.text: No file under reviewer-core/ imports from server/ (no relative escape into server, no server path alias)

assertions.rule: Hard rule 2 — keep the core pure
assertions.text: No file under reviewer-core/ imports a logger, pino, or Fastify

assertions.rule: Ports — the core receives what it needs
assertions.text: Progress leaves reviewer-core through an injected callback/port on its input (e.g. an optional onProgress handler), not by reaching out

assertions.rule: Composition — the outer ring supplies the concrete
assertions.text: The server side passes the progress handler in and writes it to the Live Log

assertions.rule: Hard rule 2 — reviewer-core performs zero I/O
assertions.text: reviewer-core still performs no network/filesystem I/O
